provenance: I authored the Unique formalization and its additional evaluation checks, but did not author Shared or the correspondence implementation. For this cross-layer review I read all required authored units, exact Lean selections and the review-policy snapshot; I also inspected the named definitions and statement assumptions in any additionally listed source context. I compared the Shared design independently, found and requested correction of a stored-mode/path-mode wording mismatch, then reread the changed shared.steps snapshot and verified other required inputs unchanged before deciding. Listing a containing source context records the inspected definitions, not an audit of every proof tactic in that file.
rationale: unit:shared.boundaries refers to the program/configuration conventions in its Given/Shared syntax and steps dependencies and to E from shared.embedding. boundary_correspondence takes an arbitrary Unique.Program, gives equality between its translated initial configuration and the translated program's Shared initial configuration, then quantifies over every Unique.Configuration. For each configuration it conjoins finished equivalence with Stuck equivalence under the fixed program.classes and its embedding. Thus the arbitrary configuration need not be reachable; the theorem is at least as general as the prose, and it does not identify stuckness with finishing. The checked initial/finished/stuck definitions retain final storage and require no remaining statement for completion, matching the claimed execution boundaries. The earlier shared.correspondence supplies the step relationship on which the boundary claim relies.
limitations: This comparison checks prose/notation and formal statement correspondence; it does not independently certify Lean proof checking or audit proof tactics.
